name: hns_xgmac_config
prose: Allocates and fills the MAC driver ops structure for an XGMAC port (hns_dsaf_xgmac.c:779-818; the packet name hns_xgmac_alloc is not the real name and the slice cut the head). mac_cb and mac_param must be valid; mac_cb->dev is used for the allocation. It allocates a zeroed struct mac_driver with devm_kzalloc(mac_cb->dev, ..., GFP_KERNEL); if that fails it returns NULL and nothing else happens. Otherwise it copies mac_id, mac_mode, io_base (from mac_param->vaddr) and dev from mac_param, stores mac_cb, fills in the XGMAC callbacks (init, enable, disable, set_mac_addr, pad/CRC config, free, tx auto pause, max frame length, pause config, info, pause enable, link status, regs, ethtool stats, sset count, regs count, strings, update_stats) and leaves set_an_mode, config_loopback, adjust_link and autoneg_stat as NULL; it returns the structure as void *. The memory is device-managed (freed with the device), not freed by the caller explicitly.
note: Slice cut the head; real function hns_xgmac_config (hns_dsaf_xgmac.c:779). Old reviewers only mechanical (right).

name: hclge_report_hw_error
prose: Forwards a hardware-error notification to the NIC client (hclge_main.c:4011-4021). It reads client = hdev->nic_client and returns without doing anything if client is NULL, or if client->ops->process_hw_error is NULL, or if HCLGE_STATE_NIC_REGISTERED is not set in hdev->state. It evaluates client->ops->process_hw_error without checking client->ops itself, so a client with a NULL ops pointer would be dereferenced. Otherwise it calls client->ops->process_hw_error(&hdev->vport[0].nic, type) and returns nothing.
note: Reviewers: original (omits NIC_REGISTERED check) right for the old prose; round-15 (code dereferences client->ops without a NULL check) right: 4016. 2/2 right.

name: UPPER_8_BITS
note: Expression macro in hinic_common.h, not a function (extracts bits 8..15 of its argument). Dropped.

name: LOWER_8_BITS
note: Expression macro in hinic_common.h, not a function (low 8 bits of its argument). Dropped.

name: hinic3_tx_poll
prose: Reclaims completed transmit descriptors of one TX queue (hinic3_tx.c:738-782; the slice shows only the tail). It reads the hardware consumer index (hinic3_get_sq_hw_ci, followed by dma_rmb()) and the local one, then loops (the body runs at least once): it stops when no further complete work request is available (hw_ci equals sw_ci or fewer WQEBBs completed than the entry's wqebb_cnt), or after HINIC3_TX_POLL_WEIGHT packets. For each completed entry it advances sw_ci, adds its WQEBB count, skb length and one packet to the totals, unmaps the skb (hinic3_tx_unmap_skb), frees it with napi_consume_skb(skb, budget) and clears tx_info->skb. Afterwards it releases the accumulated WQEBBs to the work queue (hinic3_wq_put_wqebbs), calls netif_subqueue_completed_wake with the packet and byte counts, the free WQEBB count and txq->tx_start_thrs, and returns true exactly when the number of packets reclaimed equals HINIC3_TX_POLL_WEIGHT (the poll cap was reached), otherwise false.
note: Slice began mid-function; real function hinic3_tx_poll (hinic3_tx.c:738). Old prose said 'budget fully consumed' which is the POLL_WEIGHT cap, not the napi budget; corrected.

name: i596_interrupt
prose: Interrupt handler of the i82596 driver (lib82596.c:1127-1311; slice cut the head). dev_id is the net_device; the handler takes lp->lock (spin_lock, held to the end) and the caller must not hold it. It waits up to 100 for the SCB command to clear, reads the SCB status and sets ack_cmd = status & 0xf000. If ack_cmd is 0 it unlocks and returns IRQ_NONE. If status has bit 0x8000 or 0x2000 it walks the command queue from lp->cmd_head while the head command has STAT_C set: it unlinks it, decrements cmd_backlog, and for a transmit command updates the Tx error counters, unmaps the DMA buffer, frees the skb with dev_consume_skb_irq and marks the command free (command = 0), for a TDR command logs the result, for a configure command zeroes the command; the command structure itself is not freed. It then clears the interrupt bit (0xe000 mask) on the remaining queued commands other than the tail, sets CUC_START in ack_cmd if commands remain, and writes the SCB command pointer. If status has 0x1000 or 0x4000 it calls i596_rx(dev); and when 0x1000 is set and the interface is running it adds RX_START to ack_cmd, counts rx_errors and rx_fifo_errors and calls rebuild_rx_bufs. In all non-IRQ_NONE cases it waits again for the SCB, writes ack_cmd to the SCB command, calls ca(dev) to signal the chip, waits again, unlocks and returns IRQ_HANDLED. A status with only other bits in 0xf000 (e.g. 0x4000 alone) skips the command-queue part, and a status with only command-queue bits skips the RX part.
note: Reviewers: original (completed commands are not freed, only Tx skb consumed and command marked free) right; round-2 (dequeue only for 0x8000/0x2000, RX only for 0x1000/0x4000) right; round-15 (dequeue/clear/CUC_START only when status has 0x8000 or 0x2000) right. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 1127-1311.

name: sun3_82586_send_packet
prose: ndo_start_xmit for the Sun-3 82586 driver (sun3_82586.c:1004-1131; the slice shows the body only). If skb->len is greater than XMIT_BUFF_SIZE it prints a message, frees the skb with dev_kfree_skb and returns NETDEV_TX_OK without queuing it and without stopping the queue. Otherwise it stops the queue (netif_stop_queue). Only when the driver is built with NUM_XMIT_BUFFS > 1 does it then try test_and_set_bit on p->lock; if the lock bit was already set it logs 'Queue was locked' and returns NETDEV_TX_BUSY (the skb is not freed and the queue stays stopped); in a NUM_XMIT_BUFFS == 1 build no such lock is taken. Otherwise it pads frames shorter than ETH_ZLEN with zeros, copies the data into the transmit buffer p->xmit_cbuffs[p->xmit_count] and then, depending on the build configuration, either (NUM_XMIT_BUFFS == 1 with NO_NOPCOMMANDS) writes the buffer size and starts or resumes the command unit in a loop of up to 16 tries, freeing the skb on the first try, or (NUM_XMIT_BUFFS == 1 with NOP commands) links the transmit command into the NOP chain and frees the skb, or (NUM_XMIT_BUFFS > 1) sets up the next transmit buffer, advances p->xmit_count, wakes the queue with interrupts disabled if the buffer ring is not full, clears p->lock and frees the skb. In all of these it returns NETDEV_TX_OK (1131).
note: Reviewer (the NUM_XMIT_BUFFS==1 build never locks) is right: the lock is inside #if (NUM_XMIT_BUFFS > 1) at 1019-1023. Slice cut the head; real function starts at 1004.

name: ibmveth_open
prose: ndo_open for the IBM virtual Ethernet driver (ibmveth.c:618-770; slice cut the head; ibmveth_register_logical_lan is separate). It enables NAPI, then allocates a zeroed buffer-list page and filter-list page, a coherent receive queue sized for 1 + the sizes of all rx buffer pools, DMA-maps the two list pages, and allocates a TX long-term buffer (ibmveth_allocate_tx_ltb) for each real TX queue. It disables the VIO interrupt and registers the logical LAN with ibmveth_register_logical_lan, which itself retries once after h_free_logical_lan when a previous registration (e.g. after kexec) makes the first attempt fail. Failure of that registration returns -ENONET (after logging). It then allocates each active rx buffer pool (a failure marks that pool inactive and returns -ENOMEM), requests the IRQ (returning request_irq's error), runs an initial ibmveth_interrupt replenish, starts all TX queues and returns 0. Failures unwind through labels in this order: out_free_buffer_pools (h_free_logical_lan until not busy, then frees the active pools allocated so far), out_unmap_filter_list (unmap the filter list DMA, then free all TX LTBs), out_unmap_buffer_list, out_free_queue_mem, out_free_filter_list, out_free_buffer_list, out (napi_disable, return rc). The unwind is therefore not strictly the reverse of setup: the logical LAN is freed before the buffer pools, and the filter list DMA is unmapped before the TX LTBs. Allocation failures of the list pages, queue memory and DMA mappings return -ENOMEM (rc is preset to -ENOMEM).
note: Reviewers: round-1 (logical LAN freed before buffer pools, not reverse) right: 740-748; round-2 (a stale logical-LAN registration is handled via retry, not excluded) right: ibmveth_register_logical_lan 596-613; round-15 (filter DMA before TX LTBs) right: 749-754. 3/3 right.

name: do_hard_reset
prose: Performs a hard reset of an ibmvnic adapter (ibmvnic.c:3045-3123; slice cut the head); the caller (for example __ibmvnic_reset) is expected to hold rtnl_lock or otherwise be allowed to proceed. The reset_state argument is overwritten at the start: it is re-read from adapter->state. If that state is VNIC_REMOVING or VNIC_REMOVED it returns -EBUSY (after the out label, which restores adapter->state to reset_state because rc is non-zero, i.e. leaves it unchanged). Otherwise it turns the carrier off, records adapter->reset_reason, runs ibmvnic_cleanup, releases resources, sub-CRQs and the CRQ queue, sets adapter->state to VNIC_PROBED, re-initialises init_done, then init_crq_queue and ibmvnic_reset_init (a non-zero result from either is returned). If the state before the reset was VNIC_PROBED or VNIC_DOWN it stops there with rc 0. Otherwise it logs in (ibmvnic_login), calls init_resources, disables IRQs and sets state to VNIC_CLOSED; if the saved state was VNIC_CLOSED it stops there. Finally it opens the device with __ibmvnic_open (failure becomes IBMVNIC_OPEN_FAILED) and notifies peers. At out, if rc is non-zero, adapter->state is set back to the saved reset_state; the function returns rc, which is 0 on success.
note: Round-15 reviewer (the REMOVING/REMOVED check and -EBUSY are in __ibmvnic_reset, not do_hard_reset) is WRONG: do_hard_reset itself re-reads adapter->state at 3055 and returns -EBUSY at 3057-3059 (__ibmvnic_reset has a similar check with its own positive EBUSY). Slice cut the head; real function 3045-3123.

name: __ibmvnic_reset
prose: Workqueue handler that processes queued ibmvnic reset requests (ibmvnic.c:3214-3398; returns nothing). If adapter->state is VNIC_PROBING and probe_done does not complete within the timeout (the value 5000 is passed to wait_for_completion_timeout, i.e. 5000 jiffies, not milliseconds), it logs and requeues delayed reset work (IBMVNIC_RESET_DELAY) and returns. If the state is VNIC_REMOVING it returns. Under rwi_lock, if the reset list is non-empty it sets the 'resetting' bit with test_and_set_bit_lock; if the bit was already set it requeues the delayed work, otherwise it proceeds; if nothing is queued or it did not get the bit it returns. In the loop over queued requests (get_next_rwi) it checks the state under state_lock; if REMOVING or REMOVED it frees the request, sets rc = EBUSY (positive) and leaves the loop. It saves the adapter state once (reset_state). For VNIC_RESET_PASSIVE_INIT it calls do_passive_init under rtnl_lock and turns the carrier on on success. Else, if adapter->force_reset_recovery is set it clears failover_pending and force_reset_recovery and calls do_hard_reset (taking rtnl_lock unless wait_for_reset is set), counts consecutive failures (reset to 0 on success) and, after 3 or more consecutive failures, sleeps 60 s; there is no cap of 10 failures in this function. Otherwise it calls do_reset. It then updates last_reset_time and fetches the next request; if there is none and the last reset failed it re-uses the previous request (a retry as a hard reset), else it frees the previous request; it sets force_reset_recovery when the next request is a FAILOVER or MOBILITY reset or the previous reset failed. After the loop, if wait_for_reset is set it stores rc in reset_done_rc and completes reset_done, then clears the 'resetting' bit.
note: Reviewers: original (stops after 10 consecutive failures) WRONG for this code (3347-3354: waits 60 s after 3 failures, never stops); round-2 (timeout is 5000 jiffies) right: 3217, 3241; round-15 (force_reset_recovery branch clears only failover_pending, not force_reset_recovery) WRONG: it clears both (3322, 3327/3331). 1 right, 2 wrong.

name: failover_store
prose: sysfs store handler for the ibmvnic 'failover' attribute (ibmvnic.c:6665-6704; slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL unless sysfs_streq(buf, "1") is true, i.e. buf is the string "1" optionally followed by a single trailing newline (other whitespace or other text is rejected). Otherwise it asks the hypervisor for a session token with plpar_hcall(H_VIOCTL, ..., H_GET_SESSION_TOKEN); if that hcall returns non-zero it logs and goes to last_resort. It then calls plpar_hcall_norets(H_VIOCTL, ..., H_SESSION_ERR_DETECTED, session_token); if that returns non-zero it also goes to last_resort. After a successful H_SESSION_ERR_DETECTED it returns count. last_resort calls ibmvnic_reset(adapter, VNIC_RESET_FAILOVER) and then also returns count, so a failed hcall is not reported as an error to the writer. The only error return is -EINVAL.
note: Reviewer (sysfs_streq accepts an optional trailing newline only, not general whitespace trimming) is right: 6674. Slice cut the head; real function 6665-6704.

name: e1000_init_eeprom_params
prose: Fills in hw->eeprom for an e1000 adapter (e1000_hw.c:3438-3525; slice cut the head). It reads EECD once and, by hw->mac_type: for 82542, 82543 and 82544 sets type Microwire, word_size 64, opcode_bits 3, address_bits 6, delay 50; for 82540, 82545 and 82546 sets Microwire with opcode_bits 3, delay 50 and word_size/address_bits 256/8 or 64/6 depending on E1000_EECD_SIZE; for 82541 and 82547 uses SPI (opcode_bits 8, delay 1, page_size and address_bits 32/16 or 8/8 from E1000_EECD_ADDR_BITS) when E1000_EECD_TYPE is set, else Microwire sized by E1000_EECD_ADDR_BITS; any other mac_type leaves the fields set by this switch untouched. Afterwards, whenever eeprom->type is SPI (including a value that was already SPI before the call for a mac_type not in the switch), it sets word_size = 64, reads the EEPROM_CFG word with e1000_read_eeprom (returning that call's error if it is non-zero), extracts the size field, increments a non-zero field value by one, and sets word_size = 1 << (field + EEPROM_WORD_SIZE_SHIFT). The function returns E1000_SUCCESS (0) otherwise, or the error from e1000_read_eeprom.
note: Reviewer (default path can still modify word_size when eeprom->type is already SPI) is right: the SPI block at 3504-3523 is outside the switch. Slice cut the head; real function 3438-3525.

name: e1000_probe
prose: PCI probe for the Intel e1000 driver (e1000_main.c:915-1241; slice cut the head). It enables the device (I/O BARs only when e1000_is_need_ioport), requests the selected BARs, sets bus mastering, saves PCI state, allocates the net_device and adapter, maps BAR 0 and sets up the hw struct, picks a 64-bit DMA mask only for PCI-X hardware (else 32-bit; failure aborts), runs e1000_sw_init, optionally maps the CE4100 MDIO window, sets feature flags, initialises the EEPROM parameters, resets the hardware, validates the EEPROM checksum (an invalid checksum is logged and the MAC address is zeroed but probe continues and can still return 0), reads the MAC address, WoL settings from EEPROM and device-specific WoL exceptions, auto-detects the PHY address on CE4100 (failing with goto err_eeprom if none is found), resets the adapter, and calls register_netdev. Errors: pci_enable_device and its variants return their error directly; later failures set err (-EIO for ioremap, sw_init error, MDIO ioremap, EEPROM/PHY detection failure; -ENOMEM for alloc_etherdev; the result of pci_request_selected_regions, pci_save_state, dma_set_mask_and_coherent, e1000_sw_init or register_netdev otherwise) and jump to the matching label. err is -EIO when e1000_init_eeprom_params fails (set at line 1021 and not changed before 1071), so that path returns -EIO, not 0. The labels err_register/err_eeprom reset the PHY and unmap the flash, err_mdio_ioremap frees the tx/rx ring arrays, err_dma/err_sw_init unmap the CE4100 MDIO base and BAR 0, err_ioremap marks the adapter disabled and frees the netdev, err_alloc_etherdev releases the BARs, and err_pci_reg disables the PCI device when no adapter exists or the adapter was just marked disabled; then the function returns err. On success it prints the bus info, turns the carrier off, increments cards_found and returns 0.
note: Reviewer (init_eeprom_params failure path does not set err, may return 0) is WRONG: err = -EIO at 1021 and no assignment before the failing check at 1071-1074. Slice cut the head; real function 915-1241. The EEPROM-checksum-invalid case is the one that continues and returns 0.

name: e1000_clean_rx_irq
prose: Receive-ring cleanup for the e1000 NAPI poll (e1000_main.c:4356-4496; slice cut the head). It processes descriptors from rx_ring->next_to_clean while the descriptor has E1000_RXD_STAT_DD set and *work_done < work_to_do, incrementing *work_done for each. For each it tries a copybreak skb or builds an skb around the buffer with napi_build_skb; if that allocation fails it counts alloc_rx_buff_failed and stops the loop (that descriptor is not consumed). A frame without the EOP bit (or following one) is discarded; frames with receive errors are dropped unless TBI acceptance or NETIF_F_RXALL applies; otherwise it trims the length (minus the FCS unless NETIF_F_RXFCS), sets checksum state and hands the skb up with e1000_receive_skb. It clears the descriptor status, and refills buffers through adapter->alloc_rx_buf every E1000_RX_BUFFER_WRITE cleaned descriptors and again at the end for all unused descriptors. It sets rx_ring->next_to_clean, adds the packet and byte totals to the adapter and netdev statistics and returns 'cleaned', which is true if at least one descriptor was consumed in this call (including one dropped or discarded) and false otherwise. An skb allocation failure after earlier descriptors were consumed therefore still returns true; it returns false only if no descriptor was consumed (nothing ready, work budget exhausted before the first, or failure on the first).
note: Reviewer (skb allocation failure after earlier descriptors cleaned still returns true, not false) is right: cleaned set at 4415 only after the allocation point; return at 4495. Slice cut the head; real function 4356-4496.

name: e1000_get_eeprom
prose: ethtool get_eeprom handler of the e1000e driver (ethtool.c:494-545; slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL if eeprom->len is 0, before writing anything (so eeprom->magic is not set on that path). Otherwise it sets eeprom->magic = pdev->vendor | (pdev->device << 16), computes the word range from eeprom->offset and eeprom->len, and allocates a temporary u16 buffer (-ENOMEM on failure). It reads the NVM words with e1000_read_nvm (one call for SPI NVM, else word by word, stopping at the first error). If a read failed it fills the temporary buffer with 0xff; otherwise it converts each word from little-endian. In both cases it copies eeprom->len bytes starting at byte offset (eeprom->offset & 1) of the buffer into 'bytes', frees the buffer and returns ret_val, which is 0 or the error from e1000_read_nvm. So on a read error the caller's 'bytes' buffer is still written with 0xff values and the error is returned. The caller must supply a bytes buffer of at least eeprom->len bytes and offset + len must not overflow.
note: Reviewer (len==0 returns -EINVAL before magic is set; precondition len>=1 contradicts handled len==0) is right: 505-508. Slice cut the head; real function 494-545.

name: e1000_init_phy_workarounds_pchlan
prose: Makes the PHY of an e1000e PCH-family part accessible and resets it before the PHY type is known (ich8lan.c:334-493; slice cut the head). hw must be valid with phy.ops set; the caller must not hold the PHY semaphore (the function takes it itself). It first gates automatic PHY configuration and forces ULP to unknown/disabled (a failure there is only logged, its return value is overwritten). It then calls phy.ops.acquire; if that fails it returns that error (after the common tail, without having taken or released the semaphore). While holding the semaphore it disables the PHY retry mechanism and, by MAC type (PCH2 and newer variants, LPT and newer, PCH), checks whether the PHY is accessible, tries forcing SMBus mode (with a 50 ms wait), and as a last resort toggles LANPHYPC unless the PHY reset is blocked (phy.ops.check_reset_block non-zero sets ret_val = -E1000_ERR_PHY and skips the toggle) or, for e1000_pchlan, firmware owns the PHY (FWSM valid); on LPT and newer a PHY that is still not accessible after the toggle and clearing FORCE_SMBUS gives -E1000_ERR_PHY. It re-enables retries and releases the semaphore. Only if ret_val is still 0 does it then: log 'Reset blocked by ME' and go to the tail without resetting if check_reset_block is non-zero (ret_val stays 0, so that case returns 0 with no PHY reset); otherwise reset the PHY with e1000e_phy_hw_reset_generic (its error is returned), call check_reset_block again and return its non-zero result if the ME blocks access afterwards, and, for MTP and newer, re-acquire the semaphore and reconfigure the K1 exit timeout (an acquire failure returns that error; otherwise the return value is that of e1000_reconfigure_k1_exit_timeout). At the tail, for a non-managed 82579 (pch2lan with FWSM not valid) it sleeps 10 ms and ungates automatic PHY configuration. It returns ret_val: 0, or one of the errors named above.
note: Reviewers: original (returns 0 when reset blocked by ME without reset; semaphore not acquired/released on acquire failure) right: 447-450, 353-357; round-2 (first post-release check_reset_block failure returns 0 without resetting) right: 447-450; round-15 (post-release checks can still return errors) right: 457-471, 474-479. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 334-493.

name: e1000_tx_map
prose: Maps an skb for transmit by filling consecutive TX ring buffers (netdev.c:5575-5667; slice cut the head). tx_ring->next_to_use is the first slot; max_per_txd caps the bytes per descriptor; first is the index of the first buffer and nr_frags the fragment count. It splits the linear part (skb_headlen) into chunks of at most max_per_txd, dma-mapping each with dma_map_single, then maps every page fragment in chunks with skb_frag_dma_map, recording length, jiffies timestamp and next_to_watch per buffer and counting the descriptors used. On success it stores skb, gso segment count and byte count (bytecount = (segs - 1) * headlen + skb->len) in the last buffer_info, points buffer_info[first].next_to_watch at that last slot, and returns the number of descriptors used (count). It does not advance next_to_use. If any mapping fails it logs 'Tx DMA map failed', zeroes the failing buffer's dma field, releases the already-mapped buffers through e1000_put_txbuf(..., true) walking backwards over 'count' slots, and returns 0; the skb pointer has not been stored in any buffer at that point (it is only stored after all mappings succeed), so the skb is not freed by this function and remains with the caller.
note: Reviewer (dma_error path does not release the skb; skb only stored after all mappings succeed) is right: 5647-5649 vs 5654-5666. Slice cut the head; real function 5575-5667.

name: e1000_probe
prose: PCI probe for an Intel e1000e device (netdev.c:7371-7729; the slice shows only part of it). ent->driver_data indexes e1000_info_tbl. It optionally disables ASPM states, then calls pci_enable_device_mem and, if that fails, returns its error directly without pci_disable_device (7393-7395). Later failures set err and jump to labels, all of which end at pci_disable_device and return err: no usable 64-bit DMA mask (err_dma), pci_request_selected_regions_exclusive failing (err_pci_reg), pci_save_state failing or alloc_etherdev failing (err_alloc_etherdev, which releases the memory regions; alloc failure gives -ENOMEM), ioremap of BAR 0 failing (-EIO, err_ioremap frees the netdev), mapping the flash BAR (only when FLAG_HAS_FLASH is set, BAR 1 is a memory resource and the MAC is older than pch_spt; failure gives -EIO to err_flashmap), e1000_sw_init failing (err_sw_init), ei->get_variants failing (err_hw_init), an NVM checksum that stays invalid after 3 tries or an invalid MAC address (-EIO to err_eeprom), and register_netdev failing (err_register, which also releases hardware control unless the adapter has AMT, and removes PTP). The unwind chain is err_register, err_eeprom (reset the PHY if resets are not blocked), err_hw_init (free tx/rx ring arrays), err_sw_init (unmap flash on older MACs, reset interrupt capability), err_flashmap (unmap BAR 0), err_ioremap (free_netdev), err_alloc_etherdev (release memory regions), err_pci_reg/err_dma (pci_disable_device). On the success path it sets up netdev features and MTU range, resets the controller, reads the MAC and WoL settings from NVM (NVM read errors there are only logged), initialises PTP, resets the hardware, takes hardware control unless AMT is present, registers the netdev, turns the carrier off, prints device info, calls pm_runtime_put_noidle when pci_dev_run_wake(pdev) is true and returns 0.
note: Reviewer (flash BAR mapping also requires BAR1 IORESOURCE_MEM) is right: 7447-7449. Slice cut the head; real function 7371-7729, read in full. Same function appears as two items (this item and the next).

On the success path it sets up netdev features and MTU range, resets the controller, reads the MAC and WoL settings from NVM (NVM read errors there are only logged), initialises PTP, resets the hardware, takes hardware control unless AMT is present, registers the netdev, turns the carrier off, prints device info, calls pm_runtime_put_noidle when pci_dev_run_wake(pdev) is true and returns 0.

name: fm10k_iov_mbx
prose: Services the VF mailboxes of an fm10k PF (fm10k_iov.c:197-280; returns s32 and returns 0 on both of its return statements). If interface->iov_data is NULL (READ_ONCE check) it returns 0 at once without taking the RCU lock. Otherwise it calls rcu_read_lock, re-reads iov_data and, if it is now NULL, jumps to read_unlock (releasing the RCU lock) and returns 0. If iov_data is set it takes the mailbox lock and loops over the VF mailboxes starting from iov_data->next_vf_mbx (or from the last VF when it is 0) downwards. For each VF it processes the SM mailbox first, resets the logical port and clears the macvlan queue when the VF's glort is no longer valid, resets resources and reconnects a VF whose mailbox timed out, and then, if the SM mailbox is open and has no room for a VF message (tx_ready false), it increments hw_sm_mbx_full, schedules the service event and breaks out of the loop early, so the remaining VFs are not processed in that call; otherwise it processes that VF's mailbox. After the loop, if it broke out early it records the index to resume from in next_vf_mbx; if the loop finished and next_vf_mbx was non-zero it resets it to 0 and runs the loop once more from the top, to cover the VFs skipped earlier. It then releases the mailbox lock and the RCU lock and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original (each VF mailbox is not necessarily processed per call, early exit when SM mailbox full) right: 247-256; round-2 (RCU lock not always acquired, early return when iov_data NULL skips it) right: 204-205; round-15 (second iov_data NULL check is after rcu_read_lock, so the lock is taken then released) right: 207-213, 276-277. 3/3 right.

name: fm10k_macvlan_task
prose: Delayed-work handler that sends queued MAC/VLAN update requests to the switch manager (fm10k_pci.c:765-858; the packet name fm10k_macvlan_work is not the real name and the slice cut the head). It pops requests one at a time from interface->macvlan_requests under macvlan_lock (spin_lock_irqsave). With the mailbox lock held, for each request it first checks that the SM mailbox has room (tx_ready for FM10K_VFMBX_MSG_MTU + 5); if not, it processes the mailbox, sets __FM10K_MACVLAN_REQUEST, unlocks, puts the request back at the head of the list and stops the loop. Otherwise it dispatches by item->type to update_mc_addr, update_uc_addr or update_vlan (an unknown type does nothing), unlocks the mailbox and frees the item with kfree. When the list is empty or the loop was stopped it WARNs if __FM10K_MACVLAN_SCHED is not set, clears __FM10K_MACVLAN_SCHED (after a barrier) and, if __FM10K_MACVLAN_REQUEST is set, calls fm10k_macvlan_schedule to run again. It returns nothing.
note: Slice cut the head; real function fm10k_macvlan_task (fm10k_pci.c:765). Old reviewers only mechanical ('name not in slice'), right.

name: fm10k_configure_dglort_map_pf
prose: Programs one DGLORT decode/map entry and the queues it covers on an fm10k PF (fm10k_pf.c, function head 'static s32 fm10k_configure_dglort_map_pf' just before the shown body; the packet name fm10k_iov_assign_dglort_pf is not the real name). dglort must be non-NULL: if it is NULL, or if idx > 7, rss_l > 7, pc_l > 3, vsi_l > 6, vsi_b > 64, queue_l > 8 or queue_b >= 256, it returns FM10K_ERR_PARAM without writing any register. Otherwise it writes the TX and RX SGLORT register of each queue (starting at queue_b, glort incrementing per VSI, stopping a VSI's queue loop when the queue index reaches FM10K_MAX_QUEUES), then for each priority class sets the PC field in the TXQCTL register of its queues (read-modify-write, same index limit), builds the DGLORTDEC value (rss length, queue base, pc length, VSI base and length, queue length, optional inner-RSS enable) and the DGLORTMAP value (ANY for the default dglort index, otherwise ZERO, shifted and OR-ed with the glort), writes both registers for dglort->idx and returns 0.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name is wrong; real function fm10k_configure_dglort_map_pf (head found at fm10k_pf.c line ~499). Old reviewers mechanical only (right). Contract left empty (hardware register writes).

name: fm10k_tlv_msg_test
prose: Mailbox handler for the fm10k TLV self-test message (fm10k_tlv.c:707-850; slice cut the head). hw and mbx are the device and mailbox; results is a caller-supplied array of parsed TLV attribute pointers (index FM10K_TEST_MSG_*), NULL for absent attributes; it is not parsed inside this function except for a nested attribute, which goes into a local array. If results[FM10K_TEST_MSG_RESULT] is present it returns fm10k_tlv_attr_get_s32 of it, storing the peer's result in mbx->test_result, and sends no reply. Otherwise it checks, in order, each present attribute (string, MAC+VLAN, u8, u16, u32, u64, s8, s16, s32, s64, little-endian struct) against the expected test constants, setting err to the attribute-parse error or FM10K_ERR_INVALID_VALUE on a mismatch and stopping at the first failing one; if a nested attribute is present and parses, it restarts the same checks on the nested results. It then builds a reply message carrying err as an s32 FM10K_TEST_MSG_RESULT attribute and returns mbx->ops.enqueue_tx(hw, mbx, reply), i.e. the result of queueing the reply (not err itself).
note: Round-15 reviewer (precondition wrongly requires a caller-supplied results array; function parses msg into local results) is WRONG: results is a parameter (line 707) and is read directly at 727-830; only the nested attributes go into the local nest_results (829-840). Slice cut the head; real function 707-850.

name: i40e_sync_vsi_filters
prose: Pushes the VSI's pending MAC/VLAN filter changes and promiscuous-mode changes to the i40e firmware (i40e_main.c:2548-2881; slice cut the head). The caller must not hold vsi->mac_filter_hash_lock (the function takes it) and does not need to prevent concurrent syncs: it spins with usleep_range until it can set __I40E_VSI_SYNCING_FILTERS, and clears that bit on both exits. If I40E_VSI_FLAG_FILTER_CHANGED is set it clears it and, under the hash lock, moves filters in state REMOVE to a temporary delete list and wraps NEW filters in temporary add entries (marking them NEW_SYNC), counts VLAN filters and corrects MAC/VLAN filters (i40e_correct_mac_vlan_filters, or the VF variant for SR-IOV VSIs). If a temporary allocation fails or the correction returns non-zero, it goes to err_no_memory_locked. Outside the lock it sends the delete list to firmware (broadcast filters are handled through the broadcast-promisc call and freed) in buffer-sized batches, then the add list in batches (allocation failure of either buffer goes to err_no_memory), and moves the add results back into the hash under the lock. It recomputes active_filters, may leave overflow-promiscuous mode, and for an untrusted VF clears the overflow bit and jumps to out; otherwise it computes the overflow threshold when entering overflow promisc and updates ALLMULTI and PROMISC state in firmware, setting retval to a POSIX error if a firmware call fails. At out it sets I40E_VSI_FLAG_FILTER_CHANGED if retval is non-zero (so the sync is retried), clears the syncing bit and returns retval (0 or the last firmware error converted by i40e_aq_rc_to_posix; errors from the filter add/delete helpers can also be reported through retval for deletes). The err_no_memory paths undo the temporary delete/add list entries under the lock, set I40E_VSI_FLAG_FILTER_CHANGED, clear the syncing bit and return -ENOMEM (also when the cause was a non-zero return from the filter-correction helper); they do not reset current_netdev_flags.
note: Reviewers: original (omits side effects) right; round-2 (precondition forbids concurrent sync but code waits) right: 2574-2575; round-15 (-ENOMEM path does not set FILTER_CHANGED; it resets current_netdev_flags instead) WRONG for this code: 2878 sets I40E_VSI_FLAG_FILTER_CHANGED and nothing resets current_netdev_flags (it is only assigned at 2582). 2 right, 1 wrong. Whole 334-line function read.

name: i40e_intr
prose: Legacy/MSI interrupt handler for an i40e PF (i40e_main.c:4287-4418; slice cut the head; data is the struct i40e_pf registered with the IRQ). It reads I40E_PFINT_ICR0 and I40E_PFINT_ICR0_ENA (into ena_mask). If the INTEVENT bit of ICR0 is clear (a shared line with nothing pending) it skips all handling, goes to enable_intr and returns IRQ_NONE, but still writes ena_mask back to ICR0_ENA and, unless the PF is down (or in recovery mode), schedules the service task and re-enables ICR0. Otherwise it counts a software interrupt (when only INTEVENT is set or SWINT is set), requests a core reset on IWARP PE_CRITERR (clearing that bit from ena_mask), schedules NAPI for queue 0 unless __I40E_DOWN, and for AdminQ, MDD, VFLR (either disabling VFLR notifications or marking it pending), and GRST (records the reset type counters and sets the reset-received flags) it masks the cause in ena_mask and/or sets a pending bit for the service task. An HMC error is only logged (it does not set a pending state or schedule NAPI), a timesync event schedules ptp_extts0_work and/or reads the Tx timestamp, and a software interrupt only increments the counter. Any causes left in icr0 & ena_mask are logged as unhandled, and if that includes PE_CRITERR, PCI_EXCEPTION or ECC_ERR it sets __I40E_PF_RESET_REQUESTED and schedules the service task; the unhandled bits are removed from ena_mask. It then returns IRQ_HANDLED via enable_intr (write ena_mask back, and unless the PF is down or in recovery mode, schedule the service task and re-enable the ICR0 interrupt).
note: Reviewers: original (HMC error and SWINT do not set pending state or schedule NAPI) right; round-2 (IRQ_NONE path writes ICR0_ENA and can return IRQ_NONE) right: 4299-4300, 4410, 4417; round-15 (PE_CRITERR leftover does not set PF_RESET_REQUESTED, only PCI_EXCEPTION/ECC_ERR) WRONG: 4397 includes I40E_PFINT_ICR0_PE_CRITERR_MASK. 2 right, 1 wrong.

name: i40e_buildreg_itr
prose: Builds the value to write to a vector's DYN_CTLN register (i40e_txrx.c:2607-2647; slice cut the head). It halves interval (microseconds to 2-microsecond units) and returns the INTENA bit (bit 0), itr_idx in the ITR_INDX field (bits 3-4), and the halved interval in the INTERVAL field (bits 5-16; FIELD_PREP masks the value to 12 bits, so higher bits are dropped). itr_idx I40E_ITR_NONE (3) means 'no interval update'. When force_swint is true it also sets SWINT_TRIG (bit 2), SW_ITR_INDX_ENA (bit 24) and the SW ITR index field (bits 25-26) to I40E_SW_ITR (ITR2, value 2), i.e. an extra 0x5000004 in total. It touches no state and has no other effects.
note: Reviewers: round-1 (formal omits the FIELD_PREP interval mask) right; round-15 (formal force_swint constant 0x3800000 wrong, omits SWINT_TRIG bit) right. In addition the old contract's 0x80000000 INTENA was wrong: INTENA is bit 0 (i40e_register.h:327-328). New contract checked against register.h masks and the I40E_IDX_ITR2 = 2 enum. 2/2 right.

name: i40e_napi_poll
prose: NAPI poll callback for an i40e queue vector (i40e_txrx.c:2743-2850; slice cut the head). If the VSI is down (__I40E_VSI_DOWN) it calls napi_complete and returns 0. It cleans every Tx ring of the vector (XDP/XSK Tx or normal Tx with the given budget); a ring that did not finish clears the completion flags. If budget <= 0 (netpoll) it skips Rx and jumps into the incomplete-work tail (tx_only): there, if any Tx ring requested a writeback arm (arm_wb), it counts tx_force_wb and calls i40e_enable_wb_on_itr, then returns budget. Otherwise it divides the budget among the Rx rings (at least 1 per ring when several ring pairs) and cleans each (XSK or normal); a ring that used its whole per-ring budget marks the poll as not complete. If the poll is not complete: if the current CPU is not in the vector's affinity_mask it calls napi_complete_done, forces a writeback interrupt (i40e_force_wb) and returns budget - 1; otherwise it handles arm_wb as above and returns budget. If the poll is complete it clears arm_wb_state when the Tx ring has the WB_ON_ITR flag, calls napi_complete_done and, when that returns true, re-enables the interrupt with i40e_update_enable_itr; when it returns false (busy polling) it sets q_vector->in_busy_poll = true instead. It then returns min(work_done, budget - 1).
note: Reviewers: round-1 (prose omits the budget<=0 path which skips Rx cleaning and napi_complete_done) right: 2780-2781, 2830-2835; round-15 (says in_busy_poll=true but actual false, and enable_wb_on_itr in incomplete branch) mixed: in_busy_poll IS set to true when napi_complete_done returns false (2846-2847), but enable_wb_on_itr is used in the incomplete/tx_only branch (2831-2834). 1 right, 1 mixed. Slice cut the head.

name: i40e_vc_add_mac_addr_msg
prose: Handles a VF's ADD_ETH_ADDR virtchnl message on the i40e PF (i40e_virtchnl_pf.c:3044-3103; slice cut the head). msg is a struct virtchnl_ether_addr_list. It sets ret = -EINVAL and skips straight to the reply, before taking any lock, if the VF cannot be synchronised to I40E_VF_STATE_ACTIVE or the vsi_id is not valid for the VF. Otherwise it takes the VF LAN VSI's mac_filter_hash_lock (spin_lock_bh) and calls i40e_check_vf_permission; if that returns non-zero it unlocks and jumps to the reply with that value. It then adds each address that is not already present (i40e_find_mac / i40e_add_mac_filter) and updates the VF's recorded MAC address; if adding a filter fails it logs, sets ret = -EINVAL, unlocks and jumps to the reply, leaving the earlier addresses added. After a successful loop it unlocks and calls i40e_sync_vsi_filters(vsi), logging a failure and keeping its error in ret. At error_param it returns i40e_vc_send_msg_to_vf(vf, VIRTCHNL_OP_ADD_ETH_ADDR, ret, NULL, 0), i.e. the result of sending the status reply to the VF, not ret itself. The lock is therefore released on every path where it was taken, but is not taken at all on the first (state/vsi-id) failure.
note: Round-15 reviewer (always takes/releases the lock but permission-check failure returns before locking) is mixed: the lock is NOT taken only for the state/vsi-id failure (3053-3057); the permission-check failure occurs while holding the lock and unlocks first (3064-3070). Slice cut the head; real function 3044-3103.

name: iavf_clean_rx_irq
prose: NAPI receive cleanup for one iavf Rx ring (iavf_txrx.c:1386-1488; slice cut the head). It processes descriptors from rx_ring->next_to_clean until total_rx_packets reaches budget or a descriptor without the done bit is found. Before each descriptor, if cleaned_count >= IAVF_RX_BUFFER_WRITE it calls iavf_alloc_rx_buffers (once a refill has failed, later refills are skipped via short-circuit) and resets cleaned_count to 0; unused buffers (cleaned_count below that threshold) are not replenished when the loop ends. It builds or extends an skb from the buffer (an skb allocation failure counts alloc_buff_failed and ends the loop), continues past non-EOP descriptors, frees the skb when the RXE error bit is set, drops it when iavf_cleanup_headers fails, and otherwise fills checksum/VLAN/protocol fields, passes it up with iavf_receive_skb and counts a packet. At the end it stores the partial skb back in rx_ring->skb, updates the ring and q_vector packet/byte statistics and returns budget if any buffer refill failed (to force another poll), otherwise the number of packets received, which equals budget when the budget was exhausted.
note: Reviewers: round-1 (contract weaker than prose, omits failure path returning budget) right; round-2 (normal completion can also return budget when budget packets processed) right; round-15 (not always replenishes; only when cleaned_count >= IAVF_RX_BUFFER_WRITE) right: 1401-1405. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 1386-1488.

name: __iavf_chk_linearize
prose: Decides whether a transmit skb must be linearized because any window of consecutive fragments is smaller than gso_size (iavf_txrx.c:2046-2115; slice cut the head). It reads skb_shinfo only and has no side effects. If nr_frags is less than IAVF_MAX_BUFFER_TXD - 1 it returns false immediately. Otherwise it starts with sum = 1 - gso_size, adds the sizes of the first five fragments, and then slides a window: for each step it adds the next fragment, and if the stale (oldest) fragment is larger than IAVF_MAX_DATA_PER_TXD it subtracts its alignment padding and then whole IAVF_MAX_DATA_PER_TXD_ALIGNED units from sum (the descriptors that stale fragment used up to its last partial descriptor), and returns true as soon as sum is negative, i.e. when the running window total plus 1 is less than gso_size (the stale-fragment adjustments are applied before this test). If sum is not negative it stops when the remaining nr_frags count is used up, returning false; otherwise it subtracts the stale fragment's remaining stale_size (after the negativity check) and moves the window on.
note: Reviewers: round-1 (code uses 1 - gso_size so the test is window total + 1 < gso_size, not group < gso_size) right: 2068, 2105; round-15 (stale-fragment subtraction subtracts alignment padding and whole aligned units before the negativity check, not the remainder) right: 2091-2106, the remainder (stale_size) is subtracted only after the check at 2111. 2/2 right. Reworded to avoid imprecise window arithmetic.

name: ice_dcb_process_lldp_set_mib_change
prose: Handles an LLDP MIB-change admin-queue event on an ice PF (ice_dcb_lib.c:999-1131; the packet name ice_dcb_process_lldp_net_mib_change_event is not the real name and the slice cut the head). It returns nothing. It returns early, without taking any lock, when the PF is not DCB capable, when the DCBX mode is host (DCB_CAP_DCBX_HOST), or when the event is not for the Nearest Bridge. For a Remote-MIB event it refreshes the cached remote DCBX config (from the event if a change is pending, else from firmware, only logging a failure) and returns. For a Local-MIB event it takes pf->tc_mutex, saves the old local DCBX config, zeroes it and reloads it from the event (pending change) or from firmware (ice_get_dcb_cfg; on failure it logs and goes to out). If the new config is identical it goes to out. Otherwise it updates pf->dcbx_cap, decides with ice_dcb_need_recfg whether a reconfiguration is needed, flushes DCBNL apps, and goes to out if no reconfiguration is needed. Only when a reconfiguration is needed does it set ICE_FLAG_DCB_ENA (more than one TC) or clear it, send ice_lldp_execute_pending_mib for a pending event, take rtnl_lock, disable the affected VSIs, query the port ETS (on failure it logs and skips to unlocking rtnl), reconfigure with ice_pf_dcb_recfg and re-enable the VSIs, then unlock rtnl. At out it releases pf->tc_mutex and, if a pending event has still not been executed (the early outs), sends ice_lldp_execute_pending_mib.
note: Round-15 reviewer (DCB_ENA set/cleared only when need_reconfig, not whenever config differs) is right: 1085-1099 happen after 'if (!need_reconfig) goto out'. Slice cut the head; real function ice_dcb_process_lldp_set_mib_change (ice_dcb_lib.c:999).

name: ice_dcbnl_setapp
prose: DCBNL IEEE setapp handler for the ice driver (ice_dcb_nl.c:733-858; slice cut the head). It returns without taking pf->tc_mutex: -EINVAL if the selector is not IEEE_8021QAZ_APP_SEL_DSCP, if the FW DCB agent is active (DCB_CAP_DCBX_LLD_MANAGED), if IEEE DCBX is not enabled, if the DSCP value is >= DSCP_MAX, if the PF is in a bond, or if app->priority >= the maximum TC count; -EOPNOTSUPP if the DSCP feature is not supported. After that it takes pf->tc_mutex and calls dcb_ieee_setapp (its error is returned). If the DSCP value is already marked as user-mapped it deletes the just-added TLV again and returns -EINVAL. If the port is in VLAN QoS mode it switches the firmware to DSCP PFC mode with ice_aq_set_pfc_mode (failure returns that error, leaving the already-added TLV and the dscp_mapped bit in place) and installs default DSCP/ETS/PFC values in the desired config. It then records the new mapping and app entry in the desired config and calls ice_pf_dcb_cfg; if that returns ICE_DCB_HW_CHG_RST it calls ice_dcbnl_devreset (result ignored) and returns that value, any other return is replaced by ICE_DCB_NO_HW_CHG. It always unlocks pf->tc_mutex before returning from the locked part. A failure in ice_aq_set_pfc_mode, a duplicate DSCP mapping and a dcb_ieee_setapp failure therefore leave no app recorded in the desired config; a successful return may be a non-zero ICE_DCB_* status rather than 0.
note: Previously fixed-unreviewed; the old reviewer note (omits -EINVAL on duplicate/failed setapp or PFC mode; app recorded not guaranteed) is right. Reread 733-858. Slice cut the head. Claim 'no app recorded in desired config on failure' holds for the desired config app list (new_app is appended only at 846); the IEEE app TLV from dcb_ieee_setapp is not removed on ice_aq_set_pfc_mode failure.

name: ice_dcbnl_delapp
prose: DCBNL IEEE delapp handler for the ice driver (ice_dcb_nl.c:867-969; slice cut the head). Without taking pf->tc_mutex it returns -EINVAL when the FW DCB agent is active (DCB_CAP_DCBX_LLD_MANAGED) or the PF is in a bond. Otherwise it takes pf->tc_mutex, calls dcb_ieee_delapp (its error is returned) and searches the desired config's app list for an entry with the same selector, protocol and priority; if none is found it returns -EINVAL. If found, it zeroes that entry, decrements numapps and shifts the following entries down (copying them from the local config's app array at index j + 1). If the app is not a DSCP selector or DSCP is not supported it returns ICE_DCB_HW_CHG (not 0). For a DSCP app it clears the dscp_mapped bit, remaps that DSCP value to its default priority, and if no DSCP mappings remain while in DSCP mode it switches the firmware to VLAN PFC mode (failure returns that error) and applies the default SW DCB config (ice_dcb_sw_dflt_cfg); otherwise it applies the desired config with ice_pf_dcb_cfg. If that returns ICE_DCB_HW_CHG_RST it calls ice_dcbnl_devreset; a result of ICE_DCB_NO_HW_CHG is turned into ICE_DCB_HW_CHG. It unlocks pf->tc_mutex and returns the resulting status.
note: Previously fixed-unreviewed; old reviewer note (DSCP remap only for DSCP selector with feature support; omits -EINVAL and PFC-mode failure paths) is right: 918-923, 905-908, 936-943. Note the shift copies from old_cfg (913-915) as in the code. Slice cut the head.

name: ice_cfg_tx_topo
prose: Switches the ice Tx scheduler topology between the 9-layer default and the 5-layer topology carried in a DDP package (ice_ddp.c:2388-2547; slice cut the head). Returns -EINVAL if buf is NULL or len is 0; -EOPNOTSUPP if the firmware lacks compatibility mode; -ENOMEM if the scratch buffer cannot be allocated; -EIO if the current-topology query fails, if the package fails verification, the run-time config segment is missing or has too few buffers, the section type, size (outside ICE_MIN_S_SZ..ICE_MAX_S_SZ) or offset+size (beyond ICE_PKG_BUF_SIZE) are wrong; and -EEXIST when the requested topology is already applied (9-layer default with LOAD_NEW clear, 5-layer with LOAD_NEW set) or when another PF already issued an update (after a 2 s sleep). If the topology flag says default but the layers are 5 (change 5 to 9) it skips the package parsing and goes to update_topo with an empty new topology (size 0). At update_topo it acquires the global config lock; failure returns -EBUSY before ice_deinit_hw/ice_init_hw are called. If GLGEN_RSTAT shows a reset already in progress it calls ice_check_reset and jumps to reinit_hw without applying anything, so in that case the function can return 0 (the earlier query status) after re-initialising the hardware. Otherwise it sets the new topology with ice_get_set_tx_topo (a failure becomes -EIO), always sleeps 1 s, issues a CORE reset and ice_check_reset, and reaches reinit_hw: ice_deinit_hw then ice_init_hw; if re-init fails it returns -ENODEV, otherwise it returns the status of the set operation (0 or -EIO).
note: Reviewers: original (returns 0 after reinit in the reset-in-progress path without applying topology) right: 2510-2516, 2546; round-2 (omits 0 return for the 5-to-9 default path) right as a return path is the common tail (the set status, 0 on success); round-15 (lock failure returns -EBUSY before deinit/init, contradicting 'every path that reaches update_topo') right: 2502-2507. 3/3 right. Whole function read.

name: ice_virt_get_irqs
prose: Allocates a contiguous block of MSI-X vector slots for an SR-IOV VF from the PF's virtual-IRQ tracker (ice_irq.c, 'int ice_virt_get_irqs(struct ice_pf *pf, u32 needed)'; the slice shows its tail; packet name ice_virt_alloc_irqs_tail is not a real function). It searches pf->virt_irq_tracker.bm for the first zero area of 'needed' bits (bitmap_find_next_zero_area from 0, no alignment). If the position found is not below virt_irq_tracker.num_entries it returns -ENOENT and sets nothing. Otherwise it sets those bits with bitmap_set and returns the position plus virt_irq_tracker.base, the global vector index of the first allocated vector. It takes no lock itself.
note: Slice began in the middle of ice_virt_get_irqs; fixed under the real name per rule 6 (read ice_irq.c around 236-258). The matching ice_virt_free_irqs (bitmap_clear of index - base) is a separate function also visible in the slice.

name: ice_misc_intr
prose: Handler for the ice PF 'other interrupt cause' (OICR) vector (ice_main.c:3170-3300; slice cut the head; data is the struct ice_pf). It first sets the ADMINQ, MAILBOXQ and SIDEBANDQ pending bits, then reads PFINT_OICR and PFINT_OICR_ENA (as ena_mask). For each cause: SWINT is only masked out of ena_mask and counted (no pending state bit); MAL_DETECT masks and sets the MDD pending bit; VFLR either (when VF resets are disabled) rewrites OICR_ENA with the VFLR bit cleared without touching ena_mask, or masks it and sets VFLR pending; GRST masks, counts CORER/GLOBR/EMPR resets by type (an unknown type is only logged at debug level) and, if no reset cycle was already received (test_and_set_bit of ICE_RESET_OICR_RECV), sets ICE_CORER_RECV for CORER, ICE_GLOBR_RECV for GLOBR and ICE_EMPR_RECV for every other type (including an invalid one) and sets hw->reset_ongoing; TSYN_TX is masked and its return value becomes the handler's return value (ice_ptp_ts_irq); TSYN_EVNT is masked and, if this PF owns the source timer, records the external-timestamp events. If any of PE_CRITERR, HMC_ERR or PE_PUSH is set it ORs the entire oicr value into pf->oicr_err_reg, sets ICE_AUX_ERR_PENDING and masks those bits. Remaining unmasked causes (oicr & ena_mask) are logged at debug level, and ICE_PFR_REQ is set if they include PCI_EXCEPTION or ECC_ERR. It always schedules the service task, re-enables the interrupt (ice_irq_dynamic_ena) only when the return value is IRQ_HANDLED, and returns IRQ_HANDLED unless the TSYN_TX cause replaced it.
note: Reviewers: original (SWINT/TSYN masked without pf->state pending bit; VFLR-disabled path not masked in ena_mask) right; round-2 (entire oicr ORed into oicr_err_reg, not only AUX bits) right: 3278; round-15 (invalid GRST reset type also sets ICE_EMPR_RECV) right: 3233-3234. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head.

name: ice_sched_add_rl_profile
prose: Finds or creates a rate-limit profile for a scheduler layer (ice_sched.c:3308-3374; slice cut the head); the caller is expected to hold the scheduler lock. It returns NULL if pi is NULL, if layer_num is not below pi->hw->num_tx_sched_layers (the bound is the hardware's layer count, not ICE_SCHED_MAX_LAYERS), or if rl_type is not ICE_MIN_BW, ICE_MAX_BW or ICE_SHARED_BW (mapped to CIR, EIR or SRL profile types). If the layer's rl_prof_list already holds a profile of the same type and bandwidth it returns that existing entry without any change. Otherwise it allocates a new entry with devm_kzalloc (NULL on failure), converts bw to a profile with ice_sched_bw_to_rl_profile, sets level layer_num + 1, flags and max burst size, and sends it to firmware with ice_aq_add_rl_profile. If the conversion or firmware call fails, or fewer than one profile was added, it frees the entry with devm_kfree and returns NULL; otherwise it sets prof_id_ref to 0, links the entry at the head of the layer's list and returns it.
note: Round-15 reviewer (layer_num bound is ICE_SCHED_MAX_LAYERS, not pi->hw->num_tx_sched_layers) is WRONG: 3318 uses pi->hw->num_tx_sched_layers. Slice cut the head; real function 3308-3374.

name: ice_tc_fill_rules
prose: Translates a TC flower filter into an array of switch lookup elements (ice_tc_lib.c:371-630; the packet name ice_tc_fill_fields is not the real name and the slice shows only its tail). hw, flags, tc_fltr, list and rule_info are supplied by the caller, and list must have room for every element this call writes (one for metadata, one for each selected field group). Entry 0 is the direction metadata (ice_rule_add_direction_metadata) and the next entry is the source-VSI metadata when the filter direction is egress. It sets rule_info->vlan_type to 0 first and rule_info->tun_type from the tunnel type; for a tunnel filter it adds the tunnel outer headers (ice_tc_fill_tunnel_outer) and, except for PFCP, continues with the inner headers. It then appends, in order and each only when its flag bits are set: ethertype; destination/source MAC; VLAN id and priority (outer or extended VLAN type); the VLAN TPID handling (sets rule_info->vlan_type and adds VLAN metadata, no list entry); inner C-VLAN id and priority; PPPoE session id and protocol; IPv4 or IPv6 source/destination addresses; IPv4 TOS/TTL (when the ethertype key is IP) and IPv6 traffic class/hop limit (when it is IPv6); the L2TPv3 session id; and the L4 source/destination ports, with the lookup type chosen from the IP protocol. Each group uses one list entry. It returns the number of list entries used, i.e. the final index (at least 1). The l4_proto argument is not written by this function.
note: Packet name wrong; real function ice_tc_fill_rules (371-630), read in full (the slice shows only 503-630). Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: ice_vc_process_vf_msg
prose: Dispatches one virtchnl message from a VF to the PF-side handlers (virt/virtchnl.c:2736-2936; the packet item is only the dispatch tail of this function and its name was elided). event carries the opcode, VF id, message and length; mbxdata may be NULL. It looks the VF up by id (logging and returning if there is none), takes vf->cfg_lock and releases it, together with the VF reference (ice_put_vf), at the finish label on every path that got that far. It leaves immediately (without a reply) if mbxdata is set and ice_is_malicious_vf flags the VF; if the VF is disabled (ICE_VF_STATE_DIS) it sets -EPERM; otherwise validates the message with virtchnl_vc_validate_vf_msg (mapping VIRTCHNL_STATUS_ERR_PARAM to -EPERM and any other error to -EINVAL); on any such error it replies to the VF with VIRTCHNL_STATUS_ERR_PARAM, logs and finishes. If the opcode is not allowed for this VF (ice_vc_is_opcode_allowed) it replies VIRTCHNL_STATUS_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED and finishes. Otherwise the switch on v_opcode calls exactly one handler from the VF's virtchnl_ops (get_ver_msg, get_vf_res_msg followed by VLAN-stripping init and a link-state notification, reset_vf, MAC add/del, queue config/enable/disable, VLAN, RSS, promiscuous, FDIR, stats, PTP ops, and so on) and stores its result in err; VIRTCHNL_OP_UNKNOWN and any unlisted opcode log 'Unsupported opcode' and send a NOT_SUPPORTED reply (err is then that send's result). A non-zero err from a handler is only logged ('PF failed to honor VF') and does not change the cleanup. The function returns nothing.
note: Item was a fragment of ice_vc_process_vf_msg (dispatch tail 2796-2936 of a function starting at 2736); fixed under the real name per rule 6. The old prose said every case runs 'exactly once' with cfg_lock released, which holds for the dispatch tail; the early-exit paths (malicious VF, disabled VF, invalid message, opcode not allowed) were missing.

name: idpf_vc_xn_exec
prose: Runs one virtchnl send/receive transaction on an idpf adapter (idpf_virtchnl.c:422-518; slice cut the head). It first calls idpf_vc_xn_pop_free, which takes vcxn_mngr->xn_bm_lock (spin_lock_bh) while looking for a free slot and releases it; if no slot is free the function returns -ENOSPC (so the bitmap lock is taken and released before that return, though no transaction slot is taken). With the transaction's own lock held it returns -ENXIO if the slot is in IDPF_VC_XN_SHUTDOWN (releasing only that lock; the slot is not pushed back to the free list on this path), or warns once if the slot is not IDLE but proceeds. It records the reply buffer and operation, sets the state to ASYNC or WAITING, and sends the mailbox message (idpf_send_mb_msg) with a salt/index cookie. If the send returns non-zero it releases the slot to the free list (idpf_vc_xn_push_free) and returns that send error. In async mode a successful send returns 0 without waiting and without releasing the slot (the reply path handles it). Otherwise it waits for completion up to timeout_ms and examines the final state under the transaction lock: SHUTDOWN returns -ENXIO (slot not released); WAITING (timed out) returns -ETIME; COMPLETED_SUCCESS returns the reply size xn->reply_sz; COMPLETED_FAILED returns -EIO; any other state WARNs once and returns -EIO. In the -ETIME, success, failure and invalid-state cases the slot is pushed back to the free list before the lock is dropped and the value returned.
note: Reviewers: original (omits invalid-state -EIO path) right: 504-508; round-2 (on -ENXIO the slot is not released) right: 436-438, 486-488 jump to only_unlock; round-15 (pop_free takes xn_bm_lock before returning -ENOSPC, so 'without taking any lock' is false) right: 373-385. 3/3 right.
